reviews.comment: The grading is wack. Quizzes worth 20% total, easy to miss one question and get a 70. Final was just another quiz but was worth 25%. It is not hard to do well if you understand the material well and always pay attention in class but she's very bad at teaching concepts. Labs are easy, but take lots of time. Hard class and poorly explained overall.

EJ is tough to keep pace with during lectures, but she's very engaging. Labs and homework were incredibly helpful and aligned with quiz and exam content very closely. Oftentimes she'll just straight-up tell you when something will be tested. She has a tendency to call people out and look over your shoulder, so lock in. Tough course, you'll be fine.

I don't think she understands her own lecture. When she was going over a quiz question with prepared answer in her hand, she still made at least 8 mistakes that were corrected by students. Then she makes excuse says she can't write and teach at the same time. And she has been teaching this class before. It's just too bad....

Worst lecturer I've had at A&M. Could never understanding what she was saying. Need reexplaining or an answer to a question? Then get ready to feel the weight of your parents' disappointment once again, because she will put you on blast and make you feel awful.
reviews.ratingTags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: The class isn't hard at all, labs, homework, and pop quizzes are all guaranteed 100s. She announces quiz questions in advance and there's no midterm. She's a terrible lecturer, one of the worst you'll probably ever have. If you can get past that then the class is fine.

Easily one of the worst lecturers I've ever had. She'll spend like 20 minutes on a slide getting sidetracked and it makes it really hard to follow. But she tells you the exact problems that'll be on the quiz ahead of time and the homework and labs are pretty much guaranteed 100s. Lecture attendance isn't mandatory but lab is.
Professor could not explain the subject basics clearly. She struggled with slides which were clearly older and not updated.
reviews.ratingTags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I never rate, but this class was awful. Avoid it if you can! This is a graduate-level class, but the teacher acts like students are still in elementary school and is very rude. The class was very work intensive, with loads of work due every week. The teacher was often hard to understand and made tests difficult with little to review. Nightmare

Kim has a unique lecturing style which may conflict with the text, but she explains concepts clearly AND her exams are similar to lecture content; i.e if you understand the textbook's concepts and go to lectures and review that material, your exams and homeworks will go well. The group project was... quite large, too much work but was enlightening.
Really bad professor. I expected more from a TAMU graduate professor. Lectures are purely theoritical and it is hard to see how any of the content covered is useful. Workload is a lot. 24

reviews.ratingTags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: EJ was an excellent professor. The material was confusing but she made sure that students understood. The course had many projects which were a large part of the grade. Attendance at labs and lectures was required.
reviews.ratingTags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Honestly seemed like she was excited to be there. She went kind of fast in lecture and sometimes it was hard to understand her accent but it was manageable. Her lectures made a LOT more sense when I went back to watch her recordings.  Lots of work near the end of the semester with the project, but manageable. Class is manageable but lots of work.

She is incredibly fun in lectures. EJ gives concept examples that are pertain to her in daily lives and it helped me in visualizing some architectural concepts. I can't think about memories without being reminded of her housekeeper examples. Last advice: do not team up with only 2 group members for the final project.

I ended up with a 99% average in the class with relatively little studying so I can't complain too much, but EJ has an accent that I struggled to understand all year, and our in-lecture pop quizzes relied on almost exclusively spoken questions. The labs are difficult but manageable and the tests are almost identical to HW/pop quiz questions.

Professor EJ is a good professor who wants you to learn. She does have a bit of an accent and it can be hard to understand sometimes. The lectures can be long and confusing, but once you do the HW it makes a lot more sense. This class was super interesting, but as a CPSC student hardware components are the bane of my existence.
ngl this class is horrible. it should qualify as cruel and unusual punishment. that being said I think EJ's teaching makes this class bearable.

CSCE 312 is just hard. I liked EJ, she's nice and lectures were pretty helpful all things considered. If you want to understand this class, you have to read the textbooks (I didn't lol). There's a lot of chill assignments that help offset the terrifying final. 5% grade deduction if you miss 6 labs, and every lecture has a participation assignment.
reviews.ratingTags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Group projects

reviews.comment: Do not take this professor. Lectures are impossible to consistency follow, and she acts condescending if you don't understand what to do immediately. Quizzes are graded harshly, and the final project was insane, not to mention the final that she purposely makes very difficult. Much of the work feels pointlessly tedious, expect to self study a lot.

She's very passionate, but she goes kinda fast and I felt like her class was much harder than it should've been. The in-class participation quizzes often distracted me from her lectures and made it harder to learn. She grades toughly and it's a lot of work.

Take someone else. She's condescending. She requires attendance. Her "quizzes" are realistically exams and hard. She gave us less than a month to build a virtual CPU, code it in assembly, and gave the demo on a day we don't have class right before final exams. She stated her final is hard on purpose and can drop you 2 letter grades.

HARDEST CLASS IVE EVER TAKEN! She genuinely cares about this class, but because of this her class is very hard. She is engaging during lecture, but we have an attendance "pop quiz" every day and it makes it hard to pay attention to her because she says like 5 things are on the pop quiz throughout the class. AVOID
Very difficult. You need some time. Various types of evaluation methods are used
Best professor ever, highly recommend.

I had an A+ average the whole semester until finals week. The final was ridiculous in my opinion and we didnt even know our grades until after the final grades were due in our portal (im assuming so she didnt have to deal with people asking her to curve) She selectively took away extra credit that would have saved grades. Doesnt ever communicate
reviews.ratingTags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: EJ is a great professor who really cares about her students' learning. She frequently does in-class examples with students and makes jokes. This is a difficult class with lots of work, but EJ makes it doable with her lectures and upbeat personality. Graded on a couple quizzes and homeworks, and the labs which are the bulk of the class.

Great professor. Uses analogies and interactive activities in-class, gives blunt but helpful feedback, cares about your learning. Her class is difficult, but that's the nature of Architecture. Highly recommend attending lecture because there's a lot to learn. Infrequent homework, and quizzes mirror it. Do your work honestly and an A is within reach

Very good class and professor. The final project was very time consuming but rewarding. Be sure to study hard for each "quiz", because they are more like exams and are worth 5-7% of the final grade each. The final is worth 20%. There are 2 group projects that are both pretty chill with a good group.

Prof is nice. Content is hard and just a lot. She explains well and tests are very similar to the hw she assigns. Labs are time consuming but teaches you the most. The final project is making a whole processor which is very cool. Overall hard but fulfilling course. TAs are great.

I think that EJ was a good teacher it's just that it was hard to get the big picture of the class until the very end. Having one big project at the end for the students to understand everything felt like a mistake, but outside of this one issue and some occasional confusion during lectures, I felt like this class was fine.

The class was pretty difficult content wise, but that wasn't because she made it hard - you can tell she genuinely cares. The labs are time consuming, but they give a ton of extra credit. The "quizzes"/exams aren't too bad, be sure to study the homework and you'll be fine. Pop quizzes are completion grades. The final was very difficult.
The class itself was really difficult for me. Probably the hardest class I took in the program yet. I attended all the lectures but could not learn anything from attending.

Class was difficult but interesting. There are "pop quizzes" everyday, so attendance is pretty much mandatory. I feel as if there was a disconnection between lab and lecture. The TAs didn't do anything and we learned x86 in lecture, but y86 in lab which was kind of frustrating (and confusing). Labs are the most time consuming part of the class.

Dr. Kim is one of the best professors at Texas A&M. She's always willing to answer questions, and it becomes very clear that she's insanely knowledgeable. If you actually want to learn the material and are willing to put in the work, definitely take this class. Its not too hard to make an A, but you do have to do well on the final.

Nice enough lady. She can be very disorganized, and she really rushed through the material at the end of the semester. She focuses on hardware a lot more than the other professors. Labs are really irrelevant to what we learned in lecture, especially in the middle of the semester.

Kim is a sem-decent prof. She goes very quickly and can be disorganized at times. However, she has a lot of energy and will try to help you if you are having problems. She can be kind of strict though. She doesn't like you to have your computer out in class and will call you out if you are not paying attention or doing something that bothers her.

Kim is a pretty good prof. She did a great job keeping me awake at 9:35AM, and she definitely teaches you everything you need to know to do well on the quizzes and homework. My biggest complaint is that the lab assignments were irrelevant to the lectures and significantly more difficult, so I often felt like I was just doing a ton of busy work.
reviews.ratingTags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: She isn't very helpful in office hours.
Great teacher, learned so much. Very nice, understanding and supportive.
